regions.name: flow_near_wake
regions.why: The near-wake requirement volume is currently uncovered (configured_volume_coverage 0.0). This box matches the requirement bounds exactly. Level 3 gives h = 0.375/2^3 = 0.046875 m, which satisfies the required max_cell_axis_span_metres = 0.0875 m, whereas level 2 (0.09375 m) would violate it. Level 3 equals the global surface level, so no level jump is introduced at the body surface and the cells merge smoothly into the existing 0.09375 m distance shell.

regions.name: flow_far_wake
regions.why: The far-wake requirement volume is also uncovered (coverage 0.0). Level 2 gives h = 0.375/2^2 = 0.09375 m, under the required 0.175 m span cap, and is deliberately one level coarser than the near wake to bound cost of the slowly recovering deficit, matching the stated mechanism that far-wake transport is coarsenable. It is the same size as the existing 0.28125 m distance shell, so the wake box merges without a stair-step.

regions.name: flow_aft_shear_core
regions.why: Mechanism, not score-chasing: the dimensionless estimate discharges an aft-body boundary layer of about 0.0489 m, which is only ~1.04 level-3 cells (0.046875 m), so the emerging shear layer and velocity-deficit edge behind the trailing edge would be smeared over a single cell. Level 4 halves the cell to 0.0234375 m (~2 cells across the estimated discharge thickness) in the first 1.0 m of wake, where the cross-stream gradient is steepest, while leaving the rest of the near wake at level 3 and the far wake at 2. Lateral extent is kept identical to the near-wake box so the shear layer is not clipped by a lateral refinement boundary; the only level change is a single 4->3 step in streamwise direction, within n_cells_between_levels = 3. Level 4 is within +2 of the global surface level 3. This is a hypothesis-driven resolution increase expected to matter only for the near-field deficit; it is not evidence that the wake is accurately resolved.
